name: SikaTile-305 Master Lite
paste:
SIKATILE®-305 MASTER LITE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaTile®-305 Master Lite, May 2026, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikatile-305-masterlite.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaTile®-305 Master Lite where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaTile®-305 Master Lite is a hybrid light weight polymer fortified tile adheisve suitable for internal and external applications including residential pools and spas on both wall and floor substrates.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaTile®-305 Master Lite can be used as a thin-bed tile adhesive for the following applications,
    - Wall and floor tiling applications
    - Internal and external applications
    - Wet area and balcony tiling
    - Pool and spa tiling (concrete construction)
    - Under tile heating systems
    - Sika approved acoustic reduction underlayments
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Suitable Substrate Include.
    - Concrete
    - Cement-based renders and screeds
    - Suitable Sika waterproofing membranes designed to receive direct fixed tile
    - Cement boards or sheeting*
    - Existing Ceramic tiles (primed with Sikafloor-14 Prep N Prime Impact)
    - Plasterboard (internal only)
    - other suitable construction boards designed to receive tiles*
    - Ceramic & Porcelain tiles
    - Mosaic tiles
    - Quarry and Vitrafied tiles
    - Stone not sensitive to moisture and dimensionally stable
    * refer to board manufacturers strict instructions for further details and load limits
    Suitable Tile Types Include:
1.5 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaTile®-305 Master Lite
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: A HYBRID LIGHT WEIGHT POLYMER FORTIFIED TILE ADHESIVE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2026, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS ISO 13007: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - AS3958:2023: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Further Documentation (p.2).
    - AS3958: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > SUBSTRATE QUALITY (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Hybrid technology - very high coverage
    - White colour - colour may vary dependant on local sand source.
    - C2TES1 - AS ISO Performance
    - Versatile - internal, external, external, pools.
    - Flexible
    - Low VOC
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Manufactured using white cement, colour will be influence by local sand source.
    - Product declaration: C2TES1 as per AS ISO 13007
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 15kg bag
    - Shelf life: If unopened 12 months from date of manufacture.
    - Storage conditions: Store in dry cool conditions, off ground out of direct sunlight. High humidity will reduce shelf life.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturer’s instructions and or relevant Australian Standard(s) and be structurally sound, dry, clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, sealers, curing compounds, release agents and any other loose or contaminating material. Thoroughly clean old surfaces, or new surfaces that have been treated, prior to tiling. Deeply contaminated surfaces must be prepared/abraded to a clean, sound surface. Expose at least 80% of the original substrate of painted surfaces. Substrates shall meet relevant deflection standards outlined in the relevant Australian Standards (AS3958).
3.3 Substrate quality - Concrete substrates.
    - New concrete shall be 14 days old and be left with a wood float finish.
    - Steel trowel finished concrete is generally acceptable if the concrete allows water penetration.
    - Concrete above 35MPa shall be mechanically prepared.
3.4 Substrate quality - Cement board and sheeting. All boards and sheets must be fixed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and specifically designed for tiling.
3.5 Substrate quality - Screeds & mortar beds. Sand cement screeds must be installed as per relevant Australian Standards and left for a minimum 24 hours prior to tiling. Screeds may need longer drying time in cold climates.
3.6 Substrate quality - Tile on tile applications. Ensure all existing tiles are firmly fixed, loose or hollow tiles must be removed and the area repaired using a suitable Sika repair mortar. Existing tiles shall be adequately cleaned prior to the application of the primer. Existing tiles shall be primed with Sikafloor-14 Prep N Prime Impact and allowed to dry prior to tiling.
3.7 Substrate preparation. All surfaces except waterproofing membranes shall be primed prior to application.
3.8 Substrate preparation - Priming Guide.
    | Application | Primer |
    | Porous & Dense substrates | SikaTile 010 Secure prime |
    | Refer to the relevant product data sheet for the primer for additional information. | Non-porous substrates and Tile on tile | Sikafloor-14 Prep n Prime Impact |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2026, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 5.5 - 6 Litres of clean cool potable water per 15kg bag
    - Consumption: 7.5m² with a 10mm notched trowel; Coverage is dependant of surface profile and application technique.
    - Pot Life: 2 hours at 23° degrees and 50% relative humidity. Adhesive may need restirring during its pot life. Restir without adding any additional water.
    - Open Time: 30 minutes at 23°C degrees and 50% relative humidity
4.3 Applied product ready for use.
    | Application | Wait Time |
    | Grouting and light foot traffic | 24 Hours |
    | Wet Area Service | 5 Days |
    | Submerged Applications ie pools | 21 Days |
    | Hot climates reduce wait times, and cool or cold climates will extend wait times. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    * Wait times are tested at 23°C and 50% relative humidity and should be used as a guide only.
4.4 Equipment.
    - Personal protective equipment
    - Mixing drill with stirrer attachment
    - Clean mixing buckets
    - Trowels
4.5 Mixing.
    - Measure recommended amount of clean cool potable water and slowing add the SikaTile®-305 Master Lite powder. Gradually stir the mixture untill it reaches a smooth lump free consistency (approximately 2 minutes).
    - Allow the mixture to stand or "slake" for 3-5 minutes then restir for an additional minute without add any aditional water.
    - Restiring during the adhesives pot life may be required, do not add any additional water, restir only.
4.6 Application.
    - Tiles shall be fixed in accordance with Australian Standards.
    - Ensure the back of tiles are from dust and contaminates.
    - Apply the adhesive with a notched trowel to the substrate to achieve minimum coverage requirement outlined in the relevant Australian Standards.
    - Adhesive notches should be applied in a single direction.
    - Apply tiles into the wet adhesive and break the adhesive notches to fully bed the tile in the adhesive layer. Ensure adequate coverage outlined in the Australlian Standards is achieved to both substrate and the back of tiles.
    - Tiles 400x400 and larger shall be back buttered as per relevant Australian Standards.
    - Clean excess adhesive out of the grout joints while the adhesive is still wet.
    - Allow the adhesive to dry and set prior to grouting.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment.
    - Tools and equipment can be cleaned with water prior to the adhesive setting.
    - Adhesive that has set will require mechanical removal.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first
    - Do not apply in temperatures above 35ºC or below 5ºC
    - Do not allow the adhesive to skin prior to laying the tiles. If the adhesive skins remove and dispose of it, then re-apply fresh adhesive
    - Not suitable for moisture sensitive stone, seek further advice from Sika technical support.
    - Not suitable for use for direct application over timber substrates. Apply a suitable screed or ceramic tile underlay over timber substrates.
    - Due to external influences efflorescence is beyond the control of the manufacturer
    - Setting times of the adhesive can be affected by site conditions, climate and could be faster or slower than specified.
    - Not suitable for applications externally above 3 meters.
    - Not suitable for fixing resin backed tile and stone. Prime resin back tiles with SikaFloor-14 Prep n prime prior to fixing, and refer to product information and limitations on the product data sheet
    - Contact Sika Australia for uses not mentioned in this document.
4.9 Further documentation. It is essential to plan the area to be tiled, with the inclusion of movement joints, in accordance with the relevant Australian Standard AS3958:2023 . Failure to do so may result in drummy or lifting tiles. Make sure normal building or surface movement is accommodated by installing movement joints as follows:
    - Over movement joints in the substrate
    - At a junction between different substrate materials
    - At fixtures interrupting the tile surface e.g. columns
    - At internal vertical corners
    - Around the perimeter of the tiling system
    - At a maximum of 4.5m centres, in a grid pattern
    - Movement joints should be kept free from dirt and adhesive
    - All movement joints can be filled with a suitable Sika sealant and suitable backing rod or backing tape

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Do not apply in temperatures above 35ºC or below 5ºC
    - Not suitable for moisture sensitive stone, seek further advice from Sika technical support.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaTile®-305 Master Lite, May 2026, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sikatile-305-masterlite.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTile®-305 Master Lite, version 14/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-sikatile-305masterlite.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
